cards.method: Heterogeneous-panel VAR/SVAR: (P)MG estimation, panel cointegration rank tests, structural identification (+MG-IRF/MG-FEVD), bootstrap IRF confidence bands
cards.when: a panel of N individuals × K macro variables (heterogeneous, a common lag p) -> a (pooled) mean-group panel VAR or a rank-restricted VECM; testing the panel cointegration rank (combining the K×N individual statistics); structural identification (recursive/ICA/proxy/long-run) with an MG-IRF & MG-FEVD; confidence bands through a panel/individual moving-block bootstrap or mean-group inference
cards.when_not: a single time series or individual (a single-country VAR or SVAR -> categories 03/04); a micro-panel regression with no VAR dynamics (-> #46/#47); a pure cross-section with no time dimension; data ingestion (a file upload — a frontend route, not a node)

alternatives.criterion: a stationary/level panel -> a mean-group VAR in levels (Canova-Ciccarelli 2013; Pesaran-Smith 1995 MG)
a cointegrated panel of known rank r -> a (pooled) mean-group rank-restricted VECM (Pesaran-Shin-Smith 1999 PMG; Breitung 2005)
an unknown cointegration rank -> a panel rank test (JO=the Johansen trace panel test; BR=Breitung pooled; SL=Saikkonen-Luetkepohl; CAIN=Arsova-Oersal); RUN IT BEFORE model=VEC in order to choose r

structural shocks: chol=recursive (a known causal ordering); cvm/dc=statistical ICA (non-gaussian shocks); iv=external instruments/a proxy; grt=long/short-run restrictions on an SVEC; -> an MG-IRF (Gambacorta et al. 2014) + an MG-FEVD

IRF confidence bands: pmb=a panel moving-block bootstrap (full inference); mg=the mean-group spread over the N individuals (fast, no bootstrap); mb=an individual moving-block bootstrap for one selected individual

output_key_fields: pv_estimate: A (the lined-up MG coefficient matrices), beta (the cointegrating matrix; VEC), dim_K/dim_N/dim_r, individuals, variables, estimator; fit=pvarx (register -> a raw_handle, a to_mcp stub)

pv_cointegration: panel_stats & panel_pvals (matrices: rows=the combination methods LRbar/Choi_P/Choi_Pm/Choi_Z, columns=r_H0=0.K-1), individual_stats/pvals, ranks_tested, combination_tests, csd_present

pv_identify: B (the (K×S) structural impact matrix, MG), irf (a data_frame V1=horizon + impulse->response columns), fevd_mg (a named list per response variable; the matrices sum to ~100 per row under full identification), shock_names; fit=pid (register -> a raw_handle)

pv_bootstrap: irf_point/irf_lower/irf_upper as frames (V1 plus the impulse-to-response columns, at the (1-level)/2 and 1-(1-level)/2 quantiles), n_boot as actually run, level, horizon, impulse_response, and the individual index for the moving-block route
interpretation_traps: the Breitung panel cointegration test FAILS when the type arrives as a vector; the wrapper enforces a scalar through a closed enum; the SL and CAIN variants ignore det_case and use 'SL_trend'

a panel-level FEVD is NOT defined — it works per individual only; fevd_mg is the mean group of the individual FEVDs; under partial identification (an instrument with fewer shocks than variables) the rows do NOT necessarily sum to 100
the mean-group IRF (the default) is the average of the INDIVIDUAL IRFs (Gambacorta et al. 2014); it is NOT the IRF of the mean-group VAR, which is a different quantity
recursive-design bootstrap bands (pmb/mb) do NOT necessarily contain the point estimate (a small-sample bias); mg gives the spread across the N individuals, NOT a genuine bootstrap
cvm/dc identification is STOCHASTIC (DEoptim/steadyICA); the pmb/mb bootstraps are too; determinism comes from seeding (identical confirmed); chol/mg use no RNG

chaining: pv_estimate -> pv_identify -> pv_bootstrap; pv_identify requires an UNIDENTIFIED fit and blocks an already-identified one; pv_bootstrap requires an identified fit; the long-run route requires a VEC fit
sources: Canova & Ciccarelli 2013 'Panel Vector Autoregressive Models: A Survey' Advances in Econometrics 32, 205-246
Pesaran & Smith 1995 'Estimating Long-Run Relationships from Dynamic Heterogeneous Panels' J. Econometrics 68, 79-113 (mean group)
Pesaran, Shin & Smith 1999 'Pooled Mean Group Estimation of Dynamic Heterogeneous Panels' JASA 94, 621-634 (PMG); Breitung 2005 Econometric Reviews 24, 151-173 (two-step panel cointegration)
Gambacorta, Hofmann & Peersman 2014 JMCB 46, 615-642 (the mean-group IRF); Herwartz & Wang 2024 J. Applied Econometrics 39(4), 620-639 (panel ICA identification)

Mertens & Ravn 2013 AER 103, 1212-1247 & Jentsch & Lunsford 2021 JBES 40, 1876-1891 (the proxy SVAR); Empting et al. 2025 (the panel proxy SVAR); Kilian 1998 REStat 80, 218-230 (bootstrap-after-bootstrap)

cards.when: short-T panels of countries or firms where the dynamics are assumed common and lags provide the instruments
cards.when_not: the time dimension is long enough for heterogeneous estimation; the slopes plainly differ across units

alternatives.criterion: slopes differ across units
short T, common dynamics
the series are persistent and difference GMM is weak

output_key_fields: params: the panel VAR coefficients
hansen_j: overidentification test
ar_tests: first- and second-order serial correlation in differences
irf, fevd: impulse responses and variance decompositions
interpretation_traps: INSTRUMENT PROLIFERATION IS THE CENTRAL PROBLEM: with many lags as instruments the Hansen test loses all power and reports a perfect p-value near 1, which is a warning sign rather than a pass
the AR(2) test in differences is the key diagnostic; a rejection means the lag structure is invalid
difference GMM is weak with persistent series, which is what system GMM exists to address -- at the cost of an extra assumption
sources: Roodman 2009 (Oxford Bulletin of Economics and Statistics 71:135)

cards.when: testing causality across a panel where the relationship may hold in some units and not others
cards.when_not: the panel has strong cross-sectional dependence and no bootstrap is used; there is one unit

alternatives.criterion: homogeneity assumed
heterogeneous causality across units
cross-sectional dependence is present

output_key_fields: w_bar, z_bar: the average and standardised statistics
unit_statistics: the per-unit Wald statistics
share_causal: the fraction of units showing causality
bootstrap_p: p-value robust to cross-sectional dependence
interpretation_traps: THE NULL IS NO CAUSALITY IN ANY UNIT and the alternative is causality in SOME; rejection does not mean causality holds on average, and reporting it that way is the standard misreading
cross-sectional dependence invalidates the asymptotic distribution, and the bootstrap version is required whenever the CD test rejects
the test needs the time dimension to exceed the lag order comfortably in every unit

cards.method: Panel local projections with fixed effects and Driscoll-Kraay errors
cards.when: dynamic responses estimated across a panel without imposing a VAR structure, with inference robust to cross-sectional dependence
cards.when_not: there is one unit; the time dimension is too short for Driscoll-Kraay

alternatives.criterion: you want a full system
flexible, horizon by horizon
the shock is a staggered policy adoption

output_key_fields: irf: the panel response per horizon
conf_band: bands robust to cross-sectional dependence
n_units, n_periods: the panel dimensions
heterogeneity: response variation across groups where estimated
interpretation_traps: LOCAL-PROJECTION RESIDUALS ARE SERIALLY CORRELATED at horizons beyond one, and in a panel they are also cross-sectionally correlated -- both must be handled or the bands are far too narrow
unit fixed effects in a dynamic panel introduce Nickell bias, which is worse the shorter the time dimension
pooling imposes a common response, and the pooled estimate may describe no unit
sources: Dube, Girardi, Jorda & Taylor 2023, A local projections approach to difference-in-differences (NBER WP 31184)

cards.when: panel VAR inference assumes units are independent, and that assumption is almost always false for country panels
cards.when_not: the panel has one unit; the residuals are unavailable

alternatives.criterion: large N, small T
moderate dimensions
you want to remove the dependence rather than test it

output_key_fields: cd_statistic, p_value: the dependence test
average_correlation: mean absolute residual correlation
factor_structure: leading factors in the residuals
recommendation: whether robust inference or factor augmentation is needed
interpretation_traps: A REJECTED CD TEST INVALIDATES THE STANDARD PANEL VAR STANDARD ERRORS, and continuing to report them is the most common error in applied panel VAR work
the average absolute correlation is the informative number; the test statistic conflates strength with panel size
removing dependence by cross-sectional demeaning assumes a single common factor with equal loadings, which is restrictive

cards.method: Trade-weighted foreign variables for a global VAR
cards.when: a global VAR needs each country's foreign variables built from trade or financial weights, and those weights determine the whole transmission structure
cards.when_not: there is a single country; no weight matrix is available

alternatives.criterion: simple, transparent
trade patterns changed materially over the sample
the transmission channel is financial rather than trade

output_key_fields: foreign_variables: the constructed star variables per country
weights: the weight matrix used, row-normalised
weight_source: trade, financial or custom
concentration: how concentrated each country's weights are
interpretation_traps: THE WEIGHT MATRIX IS THE MODEL'S TRANSMISSION STRUCTURE: results are driven by it at least as much as by the estimated coefficients, and it is usually treated as an innocuous input
weights must be row-normalised and have a zero diagonal, or a country enters its own foreign variable
fixed weights from one year impose that year's trade structure on the whole sample, which matters for long panels
sources: Pesaran, Schuermann & Weiner 2004 (Journal of Business and Economic Statistics 22:129-162)
Dees, di Mauro, Pesaran & Smith 2007 (Journal of Applied Econometrics 22:1)

arguments.name: fit
arguments.description: Handle to an IDENTIFIED panel SVAR (pv_identify.fit).

arguments.name: method
arguments.description: Bands (default pmb): pmb=panel moving-block bootstrap· mg=mean-group inference (spread of N individuals); mb=individual moving-block bootstrap of one individual.

arguments.name: n_boot
arguments.description: Bootstrap iterations for pmb/mb (positive integer; default 100).

arguments.name: b_length
arguments.description: method='mb': residual block length (positive integer; default 1; ~T/10).

arguments.name: b_dim
arguments.description: method='pmb': block dimensions (temporal, cross-sectional); default [1,1] i.i.d.

arguments.name: individual
arguments.description: method='mb': individual to bootstrap (name or position 1..N).

arguments.name: df
arguments.description: Handle to a long panel DataFrame {id_col + K variables}, as in pv_estimate.

arguments.name: variables
arguments.description: Names of the K (>=2) endogenous columns in system order.

arguments.name: lags
arguments.description: Common lag order p (positive integer) of the VAR in levels.

arguments.name: test
arguments.description: Procedure (default JO): JO=Johansen trace (panel); BR=Breitung two-step pooled· SL=Saikkonen-Luetkepohl· CAIN=Arsova-Oersal.

arguments.name: det_case
arguments.description: Deterministic term for JO/BR (default Case1); SL/CAIN ignore it and use 'SL_trend'.

arguments.name: n_factors
arguments.description: PANIC common factors (Arsova-Oersal) for JO/SL (default inactive).

arguments.name: df
arguments.description: Handle to a long panel DataFrame: identity column `id_col` + K numeric variable columns (same order k=1..K in each individual); >= 2 individuals, without NA.

arguments.name: variables
arguments.description: Names of the K (>=2) endogenous columns in system order.

arguments.name: lags
arguments.description: Common lag order p (positive integer) of the VAR in levels.

arguments.name: model
arguments.description: VAR = mean-group VAR in levels (default); VEC = (pooled) mean-group rank-restricted VECM.

arguments.name: type
arguments.description: Deterministic term. VAR: const/trend/both/none (default const)· VEC: Case1..Case5 (default Case4).

arguments.name: dim_r
arguments.description: model='VEC': common cointegration rank r (1..K-1); required for VEC.

arguments.name: n_factors
arguments.description: Number of common factors for SUR (default inactive).

arguments.name: n_iterations
arguments.description: Maximum iterations of SUR/pooled cointegrating vectors (default inactive).

arguments.name: fit
arguments.description: Handle to an UNIDENTIFIED panel VAR/VEC (pv_estimate.fit).

arguments.name: method
arguments.description: Identification (default chol): chol=recursive/Cholesky; cvm=Cramer-von Mises ICA· dc=distance-covariance ICA· iv=proxy/IV; grt=SVEC long/short-run (REQUIRES a VEC fit).

arguments.name: order_k
arguments.description: method='chol': causal ordering (variable names or integer positions).

arguments.name: combine
arguments.description: cvm/dc: group/pool/indiv (default indiv)· iv: pool/indiv (default pool); combination of individuals.

arguments.name: iv
arguments.description: method='iv': handle to a proxy DataFrame (L columns, T-lags rows).

arguments.name: S2
arguments.description: method='iv' with multiple proxies: MR/JL/NQ (default MR; pool=>NQ).

arguments.name: cov_u
arguments.description: method='iv': residual covariance OMEGA (÷T) or SIGMA (÷T-n) (default OMEGA).

arguments.name: n_factors
arguments.description: cvm/dc combine='group': number of common structural shocks (default inactive).

arguments.name: max_instrument_lags
arguments.description: Maximum lag depth used as instruments.

arguments.name: seed
arguments.description: Seed for the random number generator.

arguments.name: n_factors
arguments.description: Factors to extract from the residuals.

arguments.name: variables
arguments.description: Variables to build foreign counterparts for.
